marie (design): quick thread — dropped a couple of Figma frames for the new create-resource form: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/forms-flow (two variants). keen on thoughts about required-field affordances + how we handle destructive confirm for the bulk-delete flow. sam (product): saw the frames, thanks. main question: inline red text under fields vs a single top-level error banner. which reduces cognitive load for users doing quick fixes? alex (eng): from infra side the inline approach maps nicely to field-level validation hooks. fewer roundtrips if we attach errors to the input. but need to watch DOM layout shift when errors appear. jordan (a11y): inline is fine but important: errors must be announced to screen readers and focusable. we should use role="alert" or aria-live="assertive" on the message container and set aria-invalid on the input. example snippet I recommend: ```html
Please enter a valid email address
``` Also ensure error appears before the submit control in source order so SRs hear it. taylor (pm): good call. Also debating required marker — asterisk vs explicit "Required" label. a11y team says asterisk alone can be ambiguous. thoughts on copy density? marie (design): proposal A = subtle asterisk + tooltip on hover that says "required"; proposal B = small persistent "Required" label under the field. A is visually lighter, B is more explicit for new users. sam (product): prefer B for critical flows where missing data causes failed jobs later. For low-risk forms A could be OK. maybe make it context-dependent? alex (eng): implementation note: if we go B we should avoid duplicating the visual weight. keep it small and avoid adding extra DOM nodes per field unless necessary. we can toggle via a form-level flag. jordan (a11y): asterisk-only is common but not sufficient for screen reader users. if we keep asterisks, add aria-required="true" on inputs. the visible label should still be explicit for keyboard-only users. marie (design): noted — I'll mock B as default for onboarding and A for advanced forms. now destructive action: bulk-delete currently triggers a modal with "Are you sure?" and a typed-confirm field. typed-confirm reduces accidental deletes but adds friction. alternatives: soft-undo (toast with undo), single modal with more explicit copy + secondary confirmation for large sets. taylor (pm): metrics: we need to reduce accidental deletes but not kill throughput. Undo is great for small sets, typed-confirm for very large (>=100) or when deleting org-level resources. maybe combine: try toast-undo for common cases, typed-confirm for heavy ops. alex (eng): toast-undo is easiest to ship and cheap on backend. typed-confirm requires extra validation and more UI. but we also need to ensure backups/soft-delete exist. jordan (a11y): typed-confirm has a11y weight: users who use assistive tech may struggle retyping a name. make sure we provide an alternative (checkbox + confirm button) and don't rely on only typed input. marie (design): copy suggestions for modal if we keep it simple: "Delete X resources? This action cannot be undone." primary button: "Delete resources" (red), secondary: "Cancel". For typed-confirm: placeholder "Type the resource name to confirm". Avoid "Are you sure?" alone. sam (product): +1 to explicit copy. Also flagging default-button order: we should keep primary on the right for desktop, left for mobile? let's keep the standard we use across console. alex (eng): agree with keeping patterns consistent. Also performance: if we show field-level inline errors with icons, let's try to use SVG sprite to avoid per-field network overhead. marie (design): small nit — microcopy for errors: prefer human tone, e.g., "Enter a valid email" vs "Invalid format". also avoid red-only indicators — add an icon and text. jordan (a11y): add high-contrast mode check. the red must have >= 4.5:1 contrast with background or provide underline + icon. ci-bot: deploy-check: linting passed on the design tokens branch. no contrast warnings flagged automatically (manual check still needed). :robot_face: marie (design): action items: 1) I'll update Figma with B-as-default + aria annotations in comments, 2) mock the toast-undo flow for small deletes, 3) write microcopy options (3 variants) for error messages and modal copy. will tag you all when ready. sam (product): thanks — can you add a short A/B plan so we can test toast-undo vs typed-confirm for mid-sized deletes? marie (design): yep, adding a tiny experiment matrix in the Figma file comments. ping me if you want different copy variants. :sparkles: alex (eng): quick follow-up: if we do persistent "Required" labels we should batch render to avoid repaint storms. I'll pair with you on the implementation.
